newsitem.title: USA: CSCE sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures were called to open mostly unchanged on Thursday, dealers said.
They do not expect the market to break out of its trading range between the recent high of 11.87 and the recent low of 11.32 cents basis October, without news of substantial physical offtake.
Wednesday, CSCE October sugar settled 0.02 cent weaker at 11.49 cents a lb, having ranged from 11.58 to 11.41 cents. The rest of the board ended 0.02 cent lower to 0.04 cent firmer.
An estimated 16,522 lots changed hands on the day.

In fundamental news, statistician F.O. Licht said world sugar output could fall by 700,000 tonnes raw value to 123.0 million tonnes in 1997/98. Global use could rise by two million tonnes, cutting world stocks by more than 1.5 million tonnes.
Czarnikow Sugar put world sugar production at 123.25 million tonnes raw value in 1997/98 and consumption at 124.37 million tonnes.
In 1996/97, global consumption reached 123.08 million tonnes and use 121.96 million tonnes.
China, meantime, could import sugar from the world market in 1998 due to higher sugar use, Czarnikow said. It put Chinese consumption at 8.65 million tonnes for the year.

In Brazil, exports could fall to six million tonnes of raw sugar in 1997/98 from about 7.30-7.40 million tonnes this season, Czarnikow said. Alcohol production is expected to fall short of the government crop plan by about 1.5 billion liters, reaching 15.2 billion liters in the 1997/98 season.
In London, white sugar futures were slightly higher in light trade Thursday. At 0843 EDT/1243 GMT, LIFFE October was up 60 cents to $323.10 and the rest of the board was trading 20-70 cents higher.
